title: Quantum Entanglement Generation and Finite-Range Spin Coupling: A Three-Axis Null Test in a Physical-Observation Dual-Axis Model
content: We study the generation of quantum entanglement between two spatially separated spins and propose a two-ion experiment to test a finite-range interaction. In a specified quantum realization of the physical–observation dual-axis (PODA) model, a low-energy expansion of a local matter–field action yields a curl-type spin source. Eliminating the quantized field modes to second order produces a cross interaction containing products of the two endpoint spin operators. We derive the resulting entanglement dynamics from an initial product state and give a measurement-based witness applicable to noisy mixed states. For one static bridge-field channel in an unbounded homogeneous background, the trace of the coupling tensor contains a nonzero contribution set by the response length. The corresponding trace vanishes for the free-space, noncontact, quasistatic magnetic dipole interaction. With finite-source contact terms retained, this distinction leads to a direct estimator: the sum of the signed exchange coefficients measured along three common orthogonal quantization axes equals the trace of the same physical coupling tensor.The proposed trapped-ion protocol specifies phase readout, a distance scan, interleaved axis settings, error calibration, and a likelihood for the raw joint counts. Entanglement certification and interaction testing are separate inferences, based on state records and the tensor trace, respectively. We examine angular errors, motion-mediated coupling, boundaries, secular reduction, and readout dynamics, and calculate the sensitivity and acquisition time for five micrometre-scale separations. An unknown constant offset and a residual inverse-cube background substantially weaken the expected constraints. The model, assumptions, derivations, and statistical criteria are given within the paper. The numerical results are conditional design forecasts, not new measurements. Converting a measured interval into constraints on PODA action parameters requires independent matching to the experimental matter and the selected field channel.
